Apertus-Recht: which version of Art. 261bis StGB does Apertus apply?

People ask chat assistants whether something they said is punishable. Apertus-Recht releases 1,980 German, French and Italian minimal-twin scenarios under Art. 261bis StGB, each verdict computed by code from pinned Fedlex texts and consistent with 57 of 57 in-scope Swiss court rulings (always-convict: 55). Without the law, Apertus v1.5 70B convicts all but at most one of 215 lawful German scenarios. Plain rules restore publicity and the exclusions they name, but not canton, disability, political opinion or the dates; the verbatim law takes the gain back. One command re-derives every number.

Track: Apertus Readiness · Track 1B (Swiss Voices, behavioural alignment) · Event: Online · Team: 444
Demo: https://apertus-recht.mi11ion.io (every scenario, its gold and Apertus's answers) · make run (Docker, CPU, no key)

Use of Apertus

  • Model: Apertus v1.5 70B; Apertus v1.5 8B (public Q4_K_M GGUF; for exploration also the SFT, RLVR, DPO and final stages, bf16 blends, Q8_0 and MLX 4-bit builds).
  • How it is used: evaluation only: forced choice, preference pairs, and free text read by three blind judges.
  • Where it runs: the 70B on Public AI through a cost-capped gateway; the 8B as the public GGUF on CPU in CI. Public AI serves the 70B under the name apertus-v1.5-8b (same output as -70b on 760 of 792 prompts; docs/builds.md).
  • Links: code https://github.com/mi11ione/apertus-recht · dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/mi11ion/apertus-recht

Use Case Description

Art. 261bis StGB [1] (Diskriminierung und Aufruf zu Hass) punishes discrimination on grounds of race, ethnicity and religion; since 1 July 2020 it also covers sexual orientation. Whether a statement is punishable turns on elements a layperson cannot check:

  • Publicity. Under BGE 130 IV 111 [2] E. 5.2, statements among family, friends or in a setting of personal trust are not public.
  • The closed list. Only race, ethnicity, religion and sexual orientation are protected.
  • The date. The article entered into force on 1 January 1995; sexual orientation is covered from 1 July 2020.
  • The dignity threshold. Under BGE 131 IV 23 [2] E. 3, degrading (Abs. 4) means denying, or at least questioning, equal worth as human beings or equal human rights; criticism that stays objective does not suffice.

A wrong answer misinforms people about their own speech, in either direction. The users are Swiss residents asking an assistant in German, French or Italian, with or without the law in context (Apertus-v1.5-8B: 698,641 downloads worldwide in the 30 days before 9 October 2026). The dataset asks not "how often is the model right" but which law it applies, element by element. Every Art. 261bis scenario (except the 162-item exploration battery) carries a note fitted to the case: on a lawful one, what "not punishable under Art. 261bis" does not mean and where to turn; on a punishable one, that this assesses the stated facts, not legal advice, and where those affected can turn.

Dataset Summary

Per language: 660 scenarios in 220 twin groups (220 base, 215 true flips, 210 placebos, 15 contested); verdicts 430 convict, 215 acquit, 15 open. Each scenario has an acceptance criterion, an item-specific chosen answer, a rejected answer and a length-matched mirror, a settled or contested label, its normative source and its element-by-element derivation. Released alongside: the scenarios retold in the first person (all three languages), 334 natural paraphrases verified blind, a dignity-threshold family (60 per language), and a second statute (Art. 179ter, 120 items).

Term Meaning
Twin a variant that changes exactly one fact of its base. A true flip changes the verdict; a placebo does not.
Rung how much law the prompt carries. R0 no law · R3 rules spelled out (the elements, a one-sentence paraphrase of BGE 130 IV 111, the closed list, and that gender identity and sex are not covered) · R4 R3 plus one sentence on the 2020 extension · R5 verbatim law (Fedlex text of Art. 261bis and Art. 2 StGB, the Regeste) · R6 R5 with an instruction to check each element. R1 and R2 are intermediate steps of R3, used in exploration. Controls: R5a R3's rules after the verbatim law; R5e the same rules after unrelated legal text of equal length.
Framing how the verdict is asked: Ja/Nein, or the verdict word ("Urteil: schuldig / nicht schuldig")
Misapplied (red) the model convicts a variant the law acquits, while it convicts the unchanged base (95% intervals); for a placebo, a change that should not matter, it stops convicting
Read-back the law the model applies, element by element, read off the twins
Family (groups per language) One-fact change of the base Tests
SET (55) public → private setting; placebo: family wording of a public statement BGE 130 IV 111 E. 5.2
CHAR (60), CHARX (20) protected → unprotected characteristic; placebo: synonym ("Hautfarbe", "Glaube") closed list
DATE_SO (35) sexual orientation 2021–25 → before 1 Jul 2020; placebo: 1 Jul / Aug 2020 AS 2020 1609, Art. 2 StGB
DATE_CTRL (25) race, ethnicity, religion → 2018–20 (placebo) and → 1993/94 over-application; entry into force
CONTESTED (15) public → fact-dependent setting (gold open) hedging
WORDING (10) another wording family; another paragraph wording invariance

Unprotected characteristics: gender identity, sex, canton, occupation, age, disability, political opinion. The wording is templated (18 act wordings, 29 settings, 33 group phrases; 44 words on average), which is what makes the twins exact; the natural paraphrases show the results do not depend on it.

What is new. To our knowledge no dataset lets one test which version of a real statute a model applies, element by element, in the three official languages; the closest work asks when models apply the wrong law [5] (sources in docs/prior-art.md):

Dataset Languages Gold One-fact twins Real amendment dates Checked against courts
LEXam [3] / SwissLegalEvals DE, EN / DE, FR, IT exam keys, LLM judges no no no
LawShift [4] ZH expert metamorphic relations yes hypothetical revisions no
TALD [5] ZH statute version cited in judgments no which version applies from judgments
OpenExempt [6] EN solver over expert encodings single-factor suites one deadline rule no
Multilingual HateCheck [7] DE, FR, IT, … by construction templated contrasts no (not legal) no
Apertus-Recht DE, FR, IT code from pinned Fedlex texts yes, with placebos 1995, 2020, Art. 2 StGB 57/57 rulings (always-convict 55)

Data Collection Method

No data was collected from people. A seeded generator renders the scenarios from YAML templates; a 100-line engine computes each verdict from an element model of the statute whose every element cites a pinned source (Fedlex texts of Art. 261bis before and since 1 July 2020 and Art. 2 StGB in three languages, the amendment footnotes, the Regestes of BGE 130 IV 111 and 131 IV 23, each with its sha256). The engine labels each variant a true flip, placebo or contested, and the generator refuses to build if that disagrees with the design. French and Italian were translated by agents, back-translated blind and localised (Romandie, Ticino). Every change after the hash-frozen pre-registration is a timestamped amendment (prereg/AMENDMENTS.md).

Verification by re-runnable checks. Annotation ran blind, on opaque ids, without code or gold, by Claude agents and Qwen-SEA-LION-v4-32B; adjudication and legal review then checked the gold itself.

  • Annotation: six agents labelled 960 items; they agree with the code on 939/939 settled items and name the deciding element in 315/315 acquittals; a second pass that saw only the law agreed on 939/939. Qwen, given the same law-only task, agrees on 910/939; each of its 29 disagreements convicts a case the pinned text does not cover (pre-2020 sexual orientation, pre-1995, unlisted characteristics), the same errors Apertus makes.
  • Adjudication: two independent Claude agents (a third on disagreements) reviewed every disagreement, every contested item and a blind 10% sample: gold was wrong in 0 of 94 sampled items (Wilson 95% upper bound 3.9%).
  • Courts: 326 decisions citing Art. 261bis were triaged and their elements and outcome extracted twice (Cohen's κ 0.83–0.98 per field). The engine agrees with 57/57 in-scope rulings (Wilson 95% 0.94–1.00; always-convict: 55; instance level, including the Perinçek conviction later revised, 6F_6/2016), 52/52 distinct cases; the 10 genocide-denial rulings among them agree on publicity, characteristic and date only (the denial clause is not modelled). Of the two acquittals, one agrees on the court's own ground (the closed list); in the other the engine reaches the court's acquittal on a different element. Seven further rulings read the dignity threshold (agreement 6, 6 and 4 of 7, always-convict 4; reports/dignity_court.json).
  • Mutation tests (drop religion from the list, move the 2020 date by a day, make private settings public) flip exactly the items each rule governs.

Dataset Details

Quality gates (statute-twins qc, all passing): schema; gold recomputed for every item; twin invariants; no duplicates; language identity; canary; a PII scan of items, responses, metadata and the released review records (0 hits). Tests check every closed-list term and both in-force dates against the official text in three languages.

Contamination. None of the 35,241 distinct 13-grams of the core items (scan of 9 October, before the later wording amendments) occurs in the 1,069,365 decisions of voilaj/swiss-caselaw, a v1.5 pre-training source in the Apertus data catalogue; the same scan finds 846 of the 1,525 13-grams of the statute and the Regeste (positive control). The retellings, paraphrases and dignity family were written after that data was collected.

Ethics and licensing. The scenarios have no data subjects; the court-validation records are pseudonymised data on criminal proceedings from public decisions, cited by docket, naming no private person. CDLA-Permissive-2.0 with per-item licence components and provenance; legal texts public domain (Art. 5 URG); consent form with an AI-use clause; a content warning; a canary string in every item record and a scope note on every Art. 261bis scenario outside the exploration battery.

Evaluation

Three measurements on one item set.

  • Forced choice (all items at R0, R3, R4, R5, both framings; R6 German on all items, French and Italian on 240): the log-probability of the convicting answer minus the acquitting one (exact on vLLM; logits in llama.cpp).
  • Preference (settled items, R0): the same scoring between each item's chosen answer and a mirror. Two mirrors: the same sentence with the verdict and the deciding legal claim negated, and chosen word for word with only the verdict flipped.
  • Free text (240 items per language, R0, R3, R5, greedy), judged against each acceptance criterion by two Claude judges (718 of 720 German decisions agree, κ 0.993), Qwen-SEA-LION-v4-32B (694 of 718 with their consensus; κ 0.92, 0.80 on acquittals, -0.15 on 20 contested answers) and a verdict parser (698 of 700 answers with a clear verdict); a seeded 20% sample is released for audit.

The read-back. Each true flip is paired with its base, which the statute convicts. With 95% bootstrap intervals of the mean log-odds of conviction, an element is misapplied when both lie above zero; a framing in which the base itself is not convicted cannot be read. The pre-registered test fits the read-back on two wording families and predicts the third; it passes a rung if it beats the statute by at least 15 points in every readable framing.

Runs. The 70B in three languages; the 8B public Q4_K_M GGUF on CPU CI runners in three languages; Art. 179ter (120 items); the 162-item battery for training stages. Released runs record the served model and a request hash per row; the exploration runs (training stages, builds) are imported with their outputs.

Results

Pre-registered test. The locked result is Figure 1, the law each model applies, element by element. The locked held-out bar (a 15-point gain in every framing) passes trivially at R0, where the read-back is the constant "convict", and at R3 only for the 8B in Italian (16.2, interval 10.6–21.2); the German and Italian 70B reach 14.8 (10.0–18.6 and 10.5–19.5), so the 15-point bar lies inside both intervals. Post hoc: the read-back beats the statute in 21 of 22 readable cells at R3 and R4 (19 with the interval above zero) and at R3 predicts 0.94–0.98 of the 70B's held-out verdicts. Everything after this paragraph is exploratory.

Without the law, the 70B convicts nearly everything. At R0 the recall of acquittals is at most 0.01 in every language and framing (Table 2; Figure 2 shows every model by rung); Table 1 shows one twin pair. The model is not blind to the facts: its scores still rank punishable above lawful cases (AUC 0.72–0.77); the threshold sits so far on the convicting side that almost no case falls below it. Asking the other way round ("would a court acquit?") gives 0 of 215 acquittals in every language, so this is not a bias towards "yes". In free text the judges fail 73 of 75 answers to lawful scenarios as misleading (the independent judge alone: 72); every one names Art. 261bis.

With the rules spelled out (R3), publicity and the named exclusions are applied; canton, disability, political opinion and the dates are not (Figure 1):

  • Private settings are acquitted (German 70B 50 of 55), and the family-worded public placebos are still convicted (49 of 55): the model reads the setting, not the words "family" or "friends". Asked the other way round ("would a court acquit?"), it acquits 0 of 55 of them: under the rules it answers whether the elements are met and ignores the reversal (AUC 0.27). The verdict-word framing, with no Ja/Nein, confirms the gain: 47 of 55 private settings, all gender-identity and sex cases acquitted.
  • Gender identity and sex, which the prompt names as excluded, are acquitted; canton, disability and political opinion stay red in German although the prompt lists the four protected characteristics.
  • The date sentence (R4) backfires. One sentence saying that sexual orientation is protected since 1 July 2020 makes the 70B acquit the earlier cases, but also stop convicting punishable cases from 2021–25: 0 of 35 with the verdict word in German (3 with Ja/Nein). The 8B convicts 14 of 35 with Ja/Nein (19 with the verdict word). Across all punishable German scenarios the 70B convicts 22 of 125 about sexual orientation (R3: 123), against 296 of 305 about race, ethnicity and religion: the sentence does not teach the date; it takes the characteristic off the list.
  • Acts from 1993/94, before the article entered into force, are convicted by the 70B at every rung.

The verbatim law (R5) takes the gain back. Given the Fedlex text and the Regeste, as a retrieval pipeline would paste them, the German 70B acquits 0 of the 215 lawful scenarios with Ja/Nein, 1 with the verdict word; French and Italian acquit 12 and 43 (Italian keeps most private settings). The scores still separate the cases (AUC 0.77–0.80, against 0.72–0.77 at R0 and 0.84–0.89 at R3): the law moves the threshold back to "convict". In free text, 75 of 75 German answers to lawful scenarios call them punishable. It is the law's text, not its length (Table 3; McNemar p = 6·10⁻⁸), and removing the Regeste's example or adding an element check or Art. 1 StGB does not restore it (at most 16 of 75 acquitted); rules placed before the law bring back the private settings (19 of 19).

Not German-only, not the template, not one article. Free text misleads in French and Italian too (75 and 75 of 75 at R0, 75 and 66 at R5). Retold in the first person, the scenarios fare no better without the law (2 · 4 · 0 of 215 acquitted) and somewhat better with the rules (119 · 136 · 143). Natural paraphrases verified blind give 3 and 47 of 117 (templated: 2, 44). A second statute, Art. 179ter, fails in another shape: "Nein" to all 120 without the law (Ja/Nein), "schuldig" to 117 (verdict word), and with its rules (balanced 0.76) a public debate and an outsider are still convicted.

The correct reasoning does not carry the verdict. Given an item's correct answer and the same answer with only its opening verdict word flipped, the German 70B prefers the correct one on 0.85 of items, but on only 35 of 55 private settings and 64 of 100 unlisted characteristics: with the correct legal reasoning following, it still favours "punishable" for about a third of them. In Italian it is at chance on punishable items (0.50). Against a mirror that also negates the reasoning, it picks the correct answer on 0.98 (Table 4); in French it picks the correct answer on only 0.53 of the punishable items, and the 8B prefers today's list for acts before July 2020 (0.00), as its verdicts do.

Post-training and builds (8B, 162-item battery). From RLVR to DPO (one checkpoint pair), correct acquittals under stated rules fall from 185 to 146 of 220 (110 acquittals, two framings), all convictions kept; a 4-bit MLX conversion of the same DPO checkpoint agrees with it on 545 of 648 decisions, the public GGUFs of the released model on 638 (Q8_0) and 622 (Q4_K_M).

Dataset Limitations

  • Depth over breadth. One statute modelled exactly (three of its five paragraphs, the denial clause of Abs. 4 not included), with intent stated in the facts; a second statute in the same format shows the method carries over.
  • Two legal modelling choices, stated. An Abs. 2 act is also told as a one-off statement; an online post before July 2020 counts as completed on publication (dropping those items moves accuracy by 1.4 points at most).
  • Agent-run review, re-runnable from its instructions; courts, mutation tests, Qwen and the parser check from outside.

Lessons Learnt and Recommendations

  • Users: neither the bare question nor the pasted statute gives a reliable answer; plain rules help with publicity but, in German, make lawful criticism of a religion look punishable (20 of 20, Ja/Nein). For your own case, ask a counselling service or a lawyer.
  • Retrieval builders: plain rules work best alone (37 of 75 lawful items acquitted); after the pasted law they keep 11 of 75, and placed before it they bring back every private setting but lose the unlisted characteristics.
  • Developers: "the list is closed", the in-force dates and the law as written are concrete training targets.

Reproducibility

make run (Docker, CPU, no key, no model) regenerates the dataset from the YAML (sha256 per file), recomputes every result and the repaired controls and statistics from the stored responses, checks every request hash of the released runs, re-aggregates the judges, checks the pre-registration (prereg-verify: locked files, amendments, the frozen held-out code) and every claims.tsv number, and exits non-zero on any mismatch. LLM_* variables or make run-gguf add a live slice. Seeds: generator 261, bootstrap 0 (2,000 resamples). License: code Apache-2.0; dataset CDLA-Permissive-2.0; this report CC-BY-4.0.
